theme: उदार मन और आत्म-स्थिर भक्त / Noble mind and the self-settled devotee
context: This verse completes the previous one by showing that the wise devotee is not merely academically learned but inwardly settled. Krishna says that such a person is noble in spirit and receives the Lord as the supreme goal, not as a distant concept but as the very center of the self.
contextHindi: यह श्लोक पिछले श्लोक को पूरा करता है। कृष्ण यहाँ बताते हैं कि ‘ज्ञानी’ केवल पढ़ा-लिखा व्यक्ति नहीं होता; वह वह है जिसका मन भीतर से स्थिर हो गया है। ऐसे भक्त के लिए भगवान् एक दूर का सिद्धांत नहीं, बल्कि आत्मा का परम लक्ष्य बन जाते हैं।
sanskritDevanagari:
उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् |
आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ||७-१८||
transliteration:
udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tvātmaiva me matam .
āsthitaḥ sa hi yuktātmā māmevānuttamāṃ gatim ||7-18||

wordByWord.meaning: all of them; every such seeker
indeed these are such; these are all worthy
the wise one; one who knows the Lord in the deepest sense
indeed My very Self; the Lord is the inner self of such a devotee
one whose self is integrated, whose mind is steady and unified

spokenHindi: कृष्ण यहाँ कहते हैं कि ये सब भक्त बड़े उदार हैं—किसी भी रूप में भगवान् को ढूँढने वाले, वे सब महान हैं। लेकिन फिर भी सबसे महत्वपूर्ण है ‘ज्ञानी’। ‘ज्ञानी’ वह नहीं है जो सिर्फ़ सिद्धांत जानता है; वह वह है जो अपने भीतर भगवान् को स्थिरता से अनुभव करता है। ‘आत्मैव मे मतम्’—भगवान् कहते हैं, मेरे लिए ज्ञानी मनुष्य मेरे ही आत्म-समान है। यह शब्द बहुत गहरा है: ज्ञान का अर्थ मन की शुद्धता, विवेक, प्रेम और आत्म-समर्पण है। फिर कहा जाता है, ‘आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा’—वह युक्तात्मा, जिसकी आत्मा समाहित है, वही मुझे परम गति, सर्वोच्च लक्ष्य के रूप में प्राप्त करता है। इसलिए यह श्लोक न केवल बातों का सम्मान करता है, बल्कि व्यक्ति की आंतरिक स्थिति को बताता है: वह योगी वही है जो भगवान् को अपना केंद्र बनाता है।
clearEnglish: Krishna begins by affirming the dignity of all sincere seekers: noble are all these devotees. Yet he gives a further distinction: the wise one is not just one among many; for the Lord, that person is indeed His own Self, in the sense that the devotee has become inwardly aligned with divine reality. This is not anthropomorphic sentiment; it speaks of an intimacy that arises when knowledge, surrender, and steadiness merge. The phrase yuktātmā indicates a person whose intelligence is unified, whose mind is not scattered by agitation or vanity. Such a person does not chase the Divine as an external object; he or she becomes established in the Lord as the highest destination. In other words, the path is not to acquire spiritual status but to become inwardly centered, so that the Lord becomes both refuge and goal. This is the essence of mature devotion: not simply worship, but living from the truth of the divine center.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse clearly says that all sincere seekers are noble, but the wise one is specially dear to the Lord because he is integrated and established in the Lord as the supreme goal.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A valuable conclusion is that the highest maturity is not domination or status but inner steadiness. A person can be socially respectable, even outwardly religious, yet remain spiritually scattered. Krishna’s emphasis is on being yuktātmā: centered, clear, and aligned with the highest reality.

practicalApplication.label: Measure by inner steadiness
practicalApplication.text: At the end of the day, ask: 'Where was my attention today? Was I living from fear, impulse, or the wish to be seen, or was I more centered in what is true and noble?'

practicalApplication.label: Shift from identity to alignment
practicalApplication.text: Instead of asking, 'Am I spiritually advanced?' ask, 'Am I more settled, less reactive, and more available to what is good, true, and compassionate?'

reflectionQuestion: In what part of life do you still treat the Divine as a distant idea instead of the living center of your inner life?
reflectionQuestionHindi: आप अपने जीवन के किस हिस्से में भगवान् को केवल दूर की बात मानते हैं, जबकि वे आपके आंतरिक जीवन के केंद्र होने चाहिए?
